chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Sequence of record labels after Decca
summary: After Decca he recorded for Continental, Verne, Mercury, Columbia under Mitch Miller, and later Tico.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: All right, ahh, so how long did you record for Decca, then?
Oh, for Decca, we was there for a good couple of years.
All your Decca recordings then, I notice, were the 42 ones and then your next recordings were with Verne, is that right?
Yes, after Decca we recorded with gee, my memory is not too good.
Well, I got that Verne in 1945, is that right?
Yes, but before we recorded with Verne, we recorded with Continental.

Continental, and from Verne we went to - no to Mercury, and from Mercury we went with Mitch Miller. Mitch Miller joined Columbia, worked for Columbia, and then we finished with Columbia. We made all - - two-year contract we had with Columbia we made in one month, because they want to discontinue the Latin department in the United States, so from there we made a recording with Tico.
Okay, we are getting ahead of ourselves.
